items.headline: Maximum-severity unauthenticated RCE in the Feast ML feature store (CVE-2026-56121)
items.diff_narrative: A net-new top security lead with no June 25 antecedent. Yesterday's slate led with the OpenAI-Broadcom Jalapeno custom inference accelerator (June 25) and a Gartner agentic-coding-economics forecast (June 25); both drop off this run, as neither produced a fresh state-change today. Today's catalyst is a critical, unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaw in Feast, the open-source machine-learning feature store, published June 24 as CVE-2026-56121, rated CVSS 9.3 under v4.0 (9.8 on the v3.1 scale) and fixed in Feast 0.63.0. The mechanism is an unsafe-deserialization trap wired into the data plane: when the registry server processes a gRPC request, it base64-decodes the user_defined_function.body field of an OnDemandFeatureView spec and passes it straight to dill.loads() before any authorization check, so an attacker can submit a crafted serialized Python object with an arbitrary __reduce__ method and execute OS commands as the Feast service account with no credentials. The structural read is that the attack surface has moved one layer down from the model and inference engine into the ML data-and-metadata plumbing behind production feature pipelines: a registry that ingests serialized transformation logic over the network is effectively an unauthenticated code-execution endpoint unless deserialization is gated. Operators should treat any pre-0.63.0 deployment with a network-reachable gRPC endpoint as exposed, upgrade immediately, and confirm the registry is not addressable from untrusted networks, since the base64-wrapped-pickle-to-public-RPC primitive is well understood and trivially weaponizable.

items.headline: Bay Area / SV AI events calendar rolls forward; AI Engineer World's Fair is now the nearest anchor
items.diff_narrative: The forward-looking three-track events bullet carries over from June 25 with the calendar advanced. The headline change is that the events sitting at the front of yesterday's list have now reached their end and drop off the forward view: Automate 2026 (which ran through June 25 at McCormick Place), the AI Tinkerers SF Offensive Security Demo Night, and Snowflake's virtual Dev Day (both June 25) are all date-passed as of June 26. With those aged out, the nearest anchor is the AI Engineer World's Fair at Moscone West in San Francisco, opening this weekend: the official AIE World's Fair Hackathon run with Cerebral Valley fills June 27-28, an optional New Engineer Orientation runs June 28, and the main program runs June 29 through July 2 (over 20 tracks, 250+ speakers). Further out, the calendar holds unchanged across all three sub-tracks. Mainstream dev/data still lists GitHub Universe (October 28-29) and AWS re:Invent (November 30-December 4, Las Vegas). AI-security still lists Black Hat USA 2026 (August 1-6 at Mandalay Bay, with the AI Summit on Summit Day August 4 and Briefings August 5-6), DEF CON 34 and its AI Village (August 6-9), SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit (August 11-12, Half Moon Bay), OWASP Global AppSec USA (November 5-6, San Francisco), and Zenity's AI Agent Security Summit series on the watch list. AI-chip/hardware still lists AMD's Advancing AI 2026 (July 22-23 at Moscone, Instinct MI400-series keynote July 23), Hot Chips 2026 (August 23-25 at Stanford), and the AI Infra Summit (September 15-17, Santa Clara). All three sub-tracks remain covered.
